text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,514.3, up 1.14% on the day and 0.85% over the last five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 1.13% (0.13% five‑day). Advances outpaced declines (347 vs 141), giving a breadth score of 71.9 in the “HEALTHY” zone. Both indices stayed well above their 20‑day (≈72 % of stocks) and 200‑day (≈51 % of stocks) moving averages, indicating a solid rally across many stocks.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) added INR 7,411 crore today, extending a 16‑day buying streak, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 1,357 crore. The net FII futures long position is 34.1% of open interest, with a modest net short contract flow of –68,247 contracts. Sector‑wise, banks (PSU, private, financial services) and auto lead the “LEADING” quadrant, while pharma, healthcare and IT remain “LAGGING”. Options data show a put‑call ratio of 1.47 for Nifty and 1.36 for Bank Nifty, with max‑pain levels around 25,300 and 61,000 respectively; call walls sit at 26,000 (Nifty) and 64,000 (Bank Nifty).

Watch the Nifty pivot points: support at 25,241, pivot at 25,378 and resistance at 25,651. A break below 25,241 could test the 20‑day moving average (~25,200), while a move above 25,651 may push toward the call wall at 26,000. For Bank Nifty, key levels are 62,321 (S1), 62,692 (pivot) and 63,433 (R1); a breach of 62,321 could invite further buying, whereas falling through 61,000 (put wall) may trigger selling. Keep an eye on global cues such as US Nasdaq futures and crude oil prices, which have been volatile.
